testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Let rain water enter the tank.
Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.
Should never be opened.
Must stay open while the truck is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks must be drained to remove water and oil that builds up over time. If you don't drain them, the brakes can be damaged. You should manually drain the tanks at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: When steering quickly to avoid a crash, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one hand to steer.
Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
Don't use your mirrors to check other lanes.
Speed up as you get closer to the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When turning quickly to avoid hitting something in the road, always keep both hands on the steering wheel. A firm grip helps you turn fast and stay in control.

questions.question: What is removed when you drain an air tank?

options.text: Water and oil
Ammonia
Wood
Chlorine

questions.correctAnswerText: Water and oil
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains that let you remove water and compressor oil. These substances can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.

questions.question: How does fatigue affect driving?

options.text: It has little effect on driving.
It can make you a worse driver.
It is not noticeable.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you a worse driver.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous and can cause crashes. Take steps before your trip to avoid driving while fatigued.

questions.question: What should you do with your cell phone during a written exam?

options.text: Put it on airplane mode.
Turn it off.
Leave it on but place it face down.
Leave it on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn it off.
questions.explanation: All electronic devices must be turned off during a written exam.

questions.question: What does the service brake system do?

options.text: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal during normal driving.
Applies and releases the parking brakes.
Applies and releases the emergency brake.
Applies and releases the axle brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal during normal driving.
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three separate systems: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system. The service brake system works when you press the brake pedal while driving normally.

questions.question: How should cargo on flatbed trailers be secured?

options.text: Tied down.
Glued down.
Left loose.
Pushed to one side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tied down.
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers or trailers without sides, cargo must be tied down to keep it from moving or falling off during transport.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum total weight allowed for a vehicle plus its cargo
The minimum weight allowed for a trailer
The maximum weight allowed for a trailer and its cargo
The maximum weight allowed for a tractor only

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum total weight allowed for a vehicle plus its cargo
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the total weight of a vehicle plus its load. Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum combined weight allowed for a vehicle and its cargo, as set by the manufacturer.

questions.question: How can you best reduce cell phone distractions while driving?

options.text: Stay on one call for the entire trip.
Turn the phone off before driving.
Only use the phone to accept incoming calls.
Use the phone to text instead of talk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the phone off before driving.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid cell phone distractions is to turn it off before you start driving and leave it off until you reach your destination.

questions.question: The brake pedal is part of which braking system?

options.text: The service brake system
The parking brake system
The emergency brake system
The auxiliary brake system

questions.correctAnswerText: The service brake system
questions.explanation: The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: Move over laws require drivers to move away from stopped emergency vehicles. What should a driver do?

options.text: Move into a lane that is not next to the stopped vehicle.
Drive on the shoulder.
Move into the far portion of their lane.
Increase their speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into a lane that is not next to the stopped vehicle.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on a multilane road, you must move away from the lane next to it if you can do so safely. If you cannot move over safely, slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: Why should you look under your vehicle during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: To see if the vehicle is on an incline.
To check for fresh fluid leaks under the vehicle.
To see if the vehicle is in a parking spot.
To see if the vehicle is on a decline.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check for fresh fluid leaks under the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Look under your vehicle to check for fresh leaks of oil, coolant, grease, or fuel. Leaks show that your vehicle may have unsafe problems.

questions.question: When traveling across state lines, how many driver licenses should you have?

options.text: A license for each state you will visit.
A license for each state where you plan to stop.
A license for the starting state and ending state.
Only one license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only one license.
questions.explanation: You can only have one driver license. All states share driver information in a computer database to prevent people from getting more than one license.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?

options.text: Continue driving.
Drink coffee.
Stop and rest.
Drive faster to finish your trip quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy while driving, the only safe choice is to pull off the road and sleep. Stimulants like coffee are dangerous because extreme fatigue can happen when they wear off.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do in an air brake system?

options.text: They hold enough air for only one brake use.
They hold enough air to use the brakes several times if the compressor fails.
They hold air only in emergencies.
They hold enough air for more than 1,000 brake uses.

questions.correctAnswerText: They hold enough air to use the brakes several times if the compressor fails.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough air so you can use the brakes several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: Which sign shows your brakes need repair?

options.text: The brake pads have no grease on them.
The brake pads have no oil on them.
The brake pads are worn thin.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake pads are worn thin.
questions.explanation: When inspecting brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or too thin.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the safety of cargo on your vehicle?

options.text: The driver must load the cargo.
A second person can load it and is responsible for safety.
A second person can load it, but the driver is responsible for safety.
A shipping company worker must load it.

questions.correctAnswerText: A second person can load it, but the driver is responsible for safety.
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for cargo safety, no matter who loaded it onto the vehicle.

questions.question: What must you do during the vehicle inspection part of the skills test?

options.text: Explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.
Let the examiner check the vehicle.
Talk to a mechanic to show your knowledge.
Take apart the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection skills test, you must explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park your vehicle.
While you are driving.
When driving in bad weather.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park your vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must use the parking brake every time you park a vehicle with air brakes.

questions.question: What happens if a police officer stops you and you do not have your CDL with you?

options.text: You will be given a citation.
You will be put in jail.
You will lose your CDL for one year.
You will be put out-of-service for 24 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be given a citation.
questions.explanation: Driving a commercial vehicle without your CDL is a serious traffic violation. You may be cited, but you can avoid being found guilty if you show proof that you had a CDL by the deadline to pay a fine or appear in court.

questions.question: What happens if the low pressure warning light comes on while you are driving?

options.text: You can brake only if there is still enough air in the tanks.
You can apply the brakes 14 times before all the air runs out.
You can keep driving normally and check the brakes later when convenient.
You must stay at least 100 feet away from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can brake only if there is still enough air in the tanks.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop and park your vehicle as soon as possible. There may be a leak. You can still brake, but only as long as enough air remains in the tanks.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Stay in the right lane.
Have an emergency plan.
Stay in the left lane.
Drive above the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an emergency plan.
questions.explanation: While driving, watch the road ahead for hazards. Plan what you will do if a hazard becomes dangerous.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road
A thin layer of ice on the road
Ice that is black from dirt and debris
Ice that is easy to see

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road surface through it. A road with black ice may look wet but not icy.

questions.question: Which of these crimes would NOT disqualify someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Arson
Dishonesty
Robbery
Littering

questions.correctAnswerText: Littering
questions.explanation: Crimes like arson, robbery, and dishonesty disqualify you from getting a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. More serious crimes like murder result in lifetime disqualification. Littering is not a disqualifying crime.

questions.question: How long should it take for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in a dual air brake system?

options.text: Two minutes
15 seconds
10 minutes
45 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: 45 seconds
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, the air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems in about 45 seconds.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?

options.text: Air tanks
Hoses
Air lines
An air compressor

questions.correctAnswerText: An air compressor
questions.explanation: Both systems share one air compressor. If the compressor breaks, neither system will work.

questions.question: What must every air tank have in an air-braked vehicle?

options.text: A check valve
A lock
A trap door
An oxidizer

questions.correctAnswerText: A check valve
questions.explanation: All air tanks must have a one-way check valve between the air compressor and the first tank. This stops air from leaking out if there is a leak in the system.

questions.question: During an inspection, brake pads should be:

options.text: Covered in grease
Covered in coolant
Covered in oil
Free of oil and grease

questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil and grease
questions.explanation: When inspecting brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, broken shoes, or shoes worn too thin. Brake pads must be clean and dry.

questions.question: How should you hold a steering wheel?

options.text: With both hands
With one hand, keeping the other free for tasks
With one hand at a time, switching between hands
At the base of the wheel

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides.

questions.question: A cargo van carrying a light load is usually:

options.text: The same height as when fully loaded
Taller than when fully loaded
Shorter than when fully loaded
Less stable than when fully loaded

questions.correctAnswerText: Taller than when fully loaded
questions.explanation: Heavy cargo makes a vehicle sit lower. An empty vehicle is taller than a fully loaded one. If your vehicle fits under an overpass when full, it may not fit when empty.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
The weight of a tire
The weight of the air in a fully inflated tire

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the heaviest weight a tire can safely carry at a certain pressure. You can find this information on the side of the tire.

questions.question: If you operate in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, which license should you choose?

options.text: Either excepted or non-excepted
Excepted
Non-excepted
Traditional

questions.correctAnswerText: Non-excepted
questions.explanation: If you operate in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, you must get a non-excepted intrastate commerce license.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the driver's side mirror
Use both side mirrors
Not use a helper
Only use the passenger's side mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both side mirrors
questions.explanation: When backing, check both mirrors often to see hazards behind your truck. Use a helper to watch your blind spots when possible.

questions.question: Which is an example of required emergency equipment?

options.text: A supply of spare electrical fuses
A loud horn
A battery-operated flashlight
A supply of fireworks

questions.correctAnswerText: A supply of spare electrical fuses
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes: at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless your vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles (like reflective triangles).

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, you must wait for the air compressor to build a minimum of ____ in both the primary and secondary systems.

options.text: 25 psi
50 psi
75 psi
100 psi

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 psi
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, what happens if one system loses pressure?

options.text: Air from the other system will help the low-pressure system
The front or rear brakes may not work properly
All brakes will stop working
The low system will use an extra tank to refill automatically

questions.correctAnswerText: The front or rear brakes may not work properly
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one system gets very low on pressure, either the front or rear brakes may not work properly. Stop your vehicle safely and get the air system fixed.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, you should check that:

options.text: The pedal surface has been smoothed out
The gas pedal sticks
Nothing is blocking the pedals
There is something under the brake pedal

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing is blocking the pedals
questions.explanation: Check your pedals to make sure nothing blocks them. Make sure the pedals work properly and that the surfaces are grooved if needed.

questions.question: Which is NOT an example of a driver who might be a hazard?

options.text: A driver who hasn't scraped ice off the windshield
The operator of a rental truck
A driver with items covering the back windows
A person operating a pickup truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person operating a pickup truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazards. This includes drivers with ice on windshields, those with large items blocking windows, and those unfamiliar with a truck's limited rear visibility. Simply driving a pickup truck is not necessarily a hazard.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, once air pressure is lost and spring brakes engage:

options.text: You cannot move the vehicle
A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes
You can use the spring brakes to drive normally
The air tanks will automatically refill

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes
questions.explanation: A vehicle with dual parking control valves has a separate air tank. This tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they engage due to low air pressure. Pushing the correct control will release the spring brakes for a short time, letting you move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes:

options.text: Press the brake pedal
Lift the brake pedal
Pull out the brake knob
Push in the brake knob

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal
questions.explanation: To stop normally in a vehicle with air brakes, press down on the brake pedal.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, pressure of at least ____ must be built up in both braking systems.

options.text: 10 psi
25 psi
50 psi
100 psi

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 psi
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, the air compressor must build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you will be checked on traffic awareness. Which should you NOT do?

options.text: Scan the road for pedestrians.
Check traffic regularly.
Avoid checking your mirrors near intersections.
Check your mirrors regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid checking your mirrors near intersections.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, check traffic and use your mirrors regularly, especially at intersections. Always scan for pedestrians where they may be present.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
Honk your horn.
Wave to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians don't see you. Be ready for them to suddenly move into your path. You may lightly tap your horn or flash your lights as you pass.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab because of:

options.text: A defective exhaust system.
The wrong type of fuel being used.
A lack of oil in the engine.
Under-inflated tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: A defective exhaust system.
questions.explanation: A defective exhaust system is very dangerous. Poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: In bad weather, many drivers:

options.text: Like to drive in front of trucks.
Like to be on the side of trucks.
Like to follow trucks.
Like to drive without using their lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Like to follow trucks.
questions.explanation: In bad weather with poor visibility, many drivers follow closely behind trucks. Increase the distance between your vehicle and the one in front if someone is following you too closely.

questions.question: A modulating control valve can control the:

options.text: Spring brakes.
Landing gear.
Air brakes.
Anti-lock braking system (ABS).

questions.correctAnswerText: Spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver gradually apply spring brakes. The valve is controlled by a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, the vehicle:

options.text: Should be placed on an incline.
Should be placed on a decline.
May have to be running.
Should be lifted with a jack.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to be running.
questions.explanation: The engine may need to be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: When carrying cargo, you must check that it is secure:

options.text: No more than two times.
Every 150 miles or three hours of driving.
Only after traveling up a hill.
Only after coming to a hard stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles or three hours of driving.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and every three hours or 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safe and secure.

questions.question: If someone with a CDL moves to another state:

options.text: They should continue to use the license until it expires.
They can keep the license but should get a sticker for the address change.
They must retake all tests to re-certify for a CDL.
They must get a new license.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must get a new license.
questions.explanation: To drive a commercial vehicle in West Virginia, you must apply to transfer your CDL within 30 days of moving to the state.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is similar to:

options.text: Water skiing.
Flying.
Sleeping.
Walking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water skiing.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is like water skiing. Your tires glide on a film of water and lose contact with the road surface.
